messages:
ashwin: heads-up perf regression on host pre-token pipeline: saw 12-18ms tail increase for short chat requests after last kernel switch.
kevin: where in the pipeline? tokenization or batching?
marta: logs?
ashwin: digging — looks like sync prebatch stage we added for deterministic KV prewarm. repro steps:
```
curl -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/models/chat:predict -d '{"input":"hi"}'
# run 1: baseline 32QPS latency p95=45ms
# run 2 (after change) p95=62ms
```
ashwin: profiler shows extra syscall writev + grpc frame flush on transition from preparse->encode, CPU syscall time up ~6ms per request
ops-bot: deploy v2.12.4 to canary finished :party_parrot: 
kevin: looks like the prewarm work is forcing synchronous KV fetch on hot path; we intended async prefetch
ryan: I pushed a microbranch toggling async prefetch + batch coalescer, can we run quick A/B?
marta: also saw bump in KV cache miss rate on small requests — maybe shard heuristic is too eager to evict
sophia: kernel selection changed to int8-optimized path for short sequences, could that change memory layout leading to larger writev calls?
ashwin: hypothesis: prewarm writes small fragments to socket more often due to earlier flush boundary introduced by prebatch
kevin: simplest quick fix: batcher can coalesce prefetches for same session for N=10ms
ashwin: did a quick local bench: coalesce=10ms reduces p95 from 62->49ms; p50 unchanged
marta: can we toggle coalesce per route? some routes are low-latency sensitive
ryan: yes - propose sticky config: route-level coalesce with override in runtime flags
ashwin: attaching trace snippet:
```
[TRACE] req=abc123 stage=prebatch start=0ms kv_fetch=5.8ms writev=2.1ms grpc_flush=1.9ms total=58ms
```
kevin: feels like we should revert synchronous prewarm until we implement async + coalesce
marta: can we ship a canary config flip rather than revert code? less risky
ops-bot: canary config flip scheduled for 10:30 UTC
sophia: also add a kernel-selection guard: if seq_len<32 don't switch to int8 path yet
ryan: I'll open a PR for the coalesce + kernel guard, assign reviewers
ashwin: thanks — will monitor kv miss/shard hit rates after change
kevin: add a perf test to CI that simulates 1-4 token queries to catch regressions
marta: agreed. also add a small e2e watchdog that fails if p95 increases >10ms
ashwin: tl;dr: regression caused by sync prewarm + flush boundary; plan: canary config flip to async+coalesce, kernel guard, CI perf test
ryan: ACK
ops-bot: rollout started :truck: 10:30 UTC
marta: nice work catching this quickly :thumbsup:
